evidence: The original doc paragraph documents TINKERPAD_D1_DATABASE as an override yet the reversal command hardcoded 'tinkerpad'; 9becb22 rewrites it as '<database>' naming the same override, which closes the mismatch.
guidance_note: When a doc introduces an override env var, check every command in the same section that names the overridden value and parameterize it.

evidence: The original runMigration called mkdtemp with no rm on any path; 9becb22 wraps the write and D1 execute in try/finally with rm(sqlDir, {recursive, force}).
guidance_note: Pair every mkdtemp with a try/finally rm at the moment it is written, especially in a tool documented as safe to re-run.

evidence: The original migration defined its own keyOf with a comment admitting it 'Mirrors makeR2ArtifactStore's private keyOf'; 9becb22 extracts artifactObjectKey into artifactStore.ts and routes the R2 adapter, the file adapter and the migration through it.
guidance_note: When writing a comment that says code 'mirrors' a private helper elsewhere, export that helper and import it instead of copying it.

evidence: This is the same mkdtemp leak as F2 at the same line, and the same try/finally rm in 9becb22 resolves it.

runMigration had no tests. The finding named three gaps: dry-run, the missing-file precondition, and 'error propagation from spawn'. 9becb22 tested only the first two and left the wrangler write path unexercised, which round 1 flagged as F6.
guidance_note: When adding tests for an effectful executor, inject its effect seam and assert the commands it issues; don't stop at the guard paths that return before any effect.

evidence: The 9becb22 tests for F5 cover only dry-run and missing-file, and both return before the run('wrangler', ...) calls. F5 had already asked for the spawn path, so this round exists only because that fix covered part of the request; de43bf8 adds the injectable CommandRunner and asserts the exact arrays.
guidance_note: When a finding lists several untested paths, write a test for each named path before replying Fixed, and introduce an injection seam if one is needed.

evidence: The R2 put without a non-interactive flag dates from the original commit, and d6de5a4 only touched wrangler.toml, so the flag is a false positive. The concern holds because spawnRunner uses stdin 'ignore'. The agent says --yes is invalid on r2 object put and uses --force instead; the packet does not show wrangler's flag set, so which flag is correct is unverified.
guidance_note: When one wrangler command in a non-interactive runner gets a skip-prompt flag, check every other wrangler subcommand the runner spawns for its own non-interactive flag.

evidence: d6de5a4 is new provisioning work, not a named fix for any finding, so no earlier finding caused this. The runbook still said 'paste the printed database_id' after a real id was committed, which is a real inconsistency, but restoring the placeholder would have been wrong; fef24ac keeps the id and marks provisioning DONE in the comment and runbook.
guidance_note: When a commit completes a step the runbook still describes as future work, update the runbook in the same commit.

evidence: d6de5a4 uncommented routes with real hosts while the runbook still said 'uncomment routes'; the commit is new work, not a fix for a finding. fef24ac rewrites the runbook so it reports the routes as done.
guidance_note: When filling config that a runbook tells the operator to fill, search the runbook for each edited key and update the instruction.

evidence: Since round 0 the runbook told the operator to set TINKERPAD_ADMIN_SUBJECTS in [vars], but no entry existed there, so the gap is pre-existing and not caused by d6de5a4. fef24ac adds a commented placeholder with instructions.
guidance_note: When a runbook lists config keys to set, make sure each one has an entry (commented if optional) in the config file it names.

evidence: The fileExists bare catch returning false is original code that fef24ac did not touch, so the ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive. 6b66cf0 rethrows non-ENOENT errors through the shared isNotFound.
guidance_note: When writing an existence probe, narrow its catch to ENOENT with the repo's existing isNotFound helper instead of a bare catch.

evidence: This duplicates F11: the same original fileExists bare catch, untouched by fef24ac and fixed by the same 6b66cf0 change.

The original resolveConfig filters unknown args with a.startsWith('--'), so 'pnpm migrate local' silently runs a dry run; 6b66cf0 did not touch it, so the flag is a false positive. The reply is only 'Addressed in 69c85d6', and the packet does not include that commit's diff.
guidance_note: When rejecting unknown CLI input, reject every unrecognized argv entry, positional ones included, not only those that look like flags.

evidence: The leaking mkdtemp calls in the tests were added by the F5 fix in 9becb22, the same commit that fixed the identical temp-dir leak for F2 in production code. The reply is only 'Addressed in 69c85d6', and that diff is not in the packet.
guidance_note: When a commit fixes a class of leak (an mkdtemp without rm), check the new code in that same commit, tests included, for the same pattern.

evidence: From the original code the D1 upsert runs before the R2 puts, and the agent's own fef24ac comment admits a mid-upload failure would 'leave the catalog pointing at not-yet-uploaded artifacts'. 6b66cf0 did not change the order, so the flag is a false positive. The reply is only 'Addressed in 69c85d6', which the packet does not show.
guidance_note: When a multi-store write has a reference from one store into another, write the referenced objects first and the referencing index last.

evidence: The original test asserts plan.catalogDoc equals JSON.stringify(hydrateStoredDoc(JSON.parse(raw))), which repeats the function's own computation and so cannot fail. The reply is only 'Addressed in 69c85d6', which the packet does not show.
guidance_note: Assert a test's output against an independent literal or a round-trip, never against a re-run of the implementation's expression.

narrative: Round 0 raised real advisories (temp-dir leak, duplicated key convention, missing executor tests), and the agent fixed them cleanly in 9becb22. The executor-test fix covered only the guard paths, which cost round 1 (F6), and its new tests leaked temp dirs in the same way the commit had just fixed in production (F14). Round 2 came mostly from new provisioning work (d6de5a4) that left the runbook stale. Rounds 3 and 4 flagged pre-existing original code.
guidance_observations: Mid-review provisioning commits changed config without updating the runbook that described those steps, which produced three findings in one round.
Round 4's four threads got only 'Addressed in <sha>' with no plan, so the thread does not show what was done for any of them.

evidence: The reviewer concedes 'CDP should always produce parseable URLs', so the risk is theoretical. A throwing new URL() inside the listener would still leave the request neither continued nor aborted, and 2619eb5's total sameOrigin that fails closed to abort is the correct deny-by-default classification.
guidance_note: In a deny-by-default event handler, make the allow decision a total function so that unparseable input means deny.

evidence: Both builders concatenated '${contentOrigin}/...', and the handler routes on an exact pathname, so a trailing slash gives a double slash and a 404. 2619eb5 adds one originBase strip used by both builders, plus tests.
guidance_note: When building URLs by concatenating onto a configured origin, normalize the origin once and add a trailing-slash test.

evidence: This has the same root cause as F2 in playgroundThumbnailUrl, and the shared originBase in 2619eb5 covers it.

The original runBackfill skips only when thumbnails.get finds a thumbnail, so a 'failed' version is re-marked pending and re-enqueued every tick. 2619eb5 did not touch this code, so the flag is a false positive. 29cfaa1 routes the skip through renderStateOf and adds a test. Its sequential status read is what F11 then flagged.
guidance_note: When a terminal state exists, check that every producer that enqueues work consults it, the periodic backfill included.

evidence: The resolve-fault RETRY branch is original code with no test, and 2619eb5 did not touch it. 29cfaa1 adds a test with a broken catalog that asserts retry, no session call and no status.
guidance_note: When a function documents N outcome branches, write one test per branch before review.

evidence: The ack/retry and poison-pill mapping was entangled in worker.ts with puppeteer and had no tests. Rather than the edge integration test the reviewer asked for, 29cfaa1 extracts runRenderBatch over a RenderMessage seam and tests success, retry, poison and at-bound cases with fakes.
guidance_note: When writing edge glue that has branching logic, put the branching in a pure function over a structural message seam from the start so it can be tested.

evidence: The 'await context.close()' in the finally is original code that 29cfaa1 did not touch, so the flag is a false positive. A throw there would replace the successful return. 41766f8 catches and warns on both context.close and browser.close.
guidance_note: When cleanup in a finally can throw after a successful return, catch and log it so the cleanup cannot replace the result.

evidence: The '.catch(() => undefined)' was in the original handler; 2619eb5 changed only the allow expression on the line above it. 41766f8 logs the rejection at debug level before swallowing it.
guidance_note: When swallowing an error class you believe is benign, still log it, at debug level at least, so a non-benign rejection can be seen.

evidence: renderAttempt is documented 'TOTAL: never throws', yet the original awaited statuses.set('failed') unguarded, along with the put and clear. 41766f8 splits render from persistence, makes the terminal set best-effort and maps persistence faults to RETRY, with tests.
guidance_note: When documenting a function as total, walk every await in its body and make sure each rejection maps to a returned directive.

evidence: The original comment said the constant 'Mirrors the Node validator's LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS', which reads as one value with two copies. The agent says the validator uses 10_000 against 15_000 here, so they are independently tuned and should not be merged; it fixed the misleading comment in 41766f8. The validator file is not in the packet, so the 10_000 value is the agent's unverified claim.
guidance_note: Don't describe an independently tuned constant as 'mirroring' another one; say they play the same role but have separate values.

evidence: 29cfaa1, the F4 fix, added an awaited statuses.get inside the already-sequential loop, doubling the round trips to 2N; the agent admits 'The status read I added last round made the loop 2N sequential round trips.' The a8c4ba0 fix replaced it with an unbounded Promise.all, which F15 then flagged. The concurrency change is not a dataflow-vs-control-flow matter.
guidance_note: When adding a per-item I/O read inside a loop, decide the concurrency model in the same change, parallel and bounded, rather than extending a sequential await chain.

evidence: The original renderAttempt suite tested only the unlisted skip and had no already-rendered skip; 41766f8 did not touch it. a8c4ba0 adds the test with the session untouched and the thumbnail not overwritten.
guidance_note: When a function composes a discriminated union of skip reasons, test each variant at the composing function's level.

evidence: The original 'thumbnail not rendered yet' 404 had no cache-control, and its URL stays the same when the PNG lands, so a heuristically cached 404 would pin the empty slot. a8c4ba0 defaults sealed() to no-cache with an explicit opt-out for the PNG, which also covers the 410-then-relist case.
guidance_note: When a response's meaning can change for the same URL, set its cache-control explicitly, defaulting to revalidate.

evidence: The reviewer itself calls the two instances 'correct and cheap'. Both paths call the same factories, makeR2ThumbnailStore and makeD1Catalog, so an interceptor added to a factory reaches both and there is no duplicated logic to drift.

a8c4ba0, the F11 fix, introduced unbounded Promise.all fan-out. The reviewer's stated failure is exceeding '1000 per request' subrequests, a per-invocation total that is still 2N after chunking into groups of 50. The agent's mapBounded fix limits in-flight concurrency but not the hazard the finding named.
guidance_note: When a finding cites a platform limit, identify whether it caps concurrency or total count before picking the fix, because chunking only addresses the first.

evidence: The set-pending-then-enqueue order was in the original runBackfill, and a8c4ba0 kept it unchanged. With a missing status already read as pending, an interruption after the set leaves the version with no job until the next tick. Enqueuing first leaves an idempotent job with no status instead.
guidance_note: When writing a two-step side effect, order it so that an interruption leaves the load-bearing step done and the cosmetic step missing.

evidence: runBackfill had no tests of its failure paths. The agent added a test showing that an enqueue rejection propagates, the contract the scheduled() boundary relies on.
guidance_note: When a function's contract is 'propagate so the boundary logs', add a test that asserts the propagation.

evidence: The reviewer's scenario is wrong: a retry after a failed put follows a put that stored nothing, so no client cached earlier bytes. 'immutable' is still a stronger promise than thumbnailStore's 'a re-put REPLACES the bytes' allows, so dropping it is sound. The header was original code, not caused by the 41766f8 retry path, and the issue is a cache-semantics mismatch rather than a one-source-of-truth one.
guidance_note: Before promising 'immutable' on a URL, check that the backing store's contract forbids overwriting that key.

evidence: pageShell's .card-preview-img and index.html's .pg-card-preview-img carried identical rules from the original PR. The agent lifted them into PREVIEW_IMG_CSS, reusing the existing TOKENS_CSS splice-and-drift-test mechanism.
guidance_note: When adding a style to both card surfaces, use the existing shared-CSS splice mechanism (as TOKENS_CSS does) rather than writing the rule twice.

evidence: The regression the reviewer named, Cloudflare Message no longer satisfying RenderMessage, would fail typecheck at the runRenderBatch(session, pipeline, batch.messages, ...) call, and the ack/retry behavior is already tested. a8c4ba0 does not touch worker.ts, so the flag is a false positive. Leaning on the type checker is a types argument, not behavior-not-structure.

narrative: Most findings across all five rounds pointed at original PR code even when they carried ON-NAMED-FIX flags: untested branches, a finally that could replace a return, a silent catch, and cache headers. The one real chain is the backfill. Fixing the failed-status gate (F4) added a sequential read (F11), parallelizing that produced unbounded fan-out (F15), and the bounded-chunk fix still did not address the per-request total limit the reviewer cited. No round was avoidable as a whole, because each also carried independent original-code findings. The agent's two main pushbacks (F14, F20) held, and the F10 pushback holds if its unverified constant values are right.
guidance_observations: The backfill was reworked three times across rounds, each time for a different property (correctness, then latency, then fan-out). One pass that decided correctness and the concurrency model together would have removed two findings.
Many round-2 to round-4 findings were original-code gaps (untested branches, a total-contract violation) that a branch-by-branch self-review before opening the PR would have caught.
